title: JPA Relationships
summary: Map related entities and keep relationship ownership separate from cascading.

richText: Related entities
A relationship maps a reference from one entity to another entity.
@ManyToOne means many source entities can refer to one target entity. @OneToMany represents the reverse collection.
@OneToOne represents a single related entity on each side. @ManyToMany represents collections on both sides.
A foreign key is a database column that refers to a row in another table.
The owning side
The owning side controls the stored relationship. For a bidirectional one-to-many mapping, the many-to-one side owns the foreign key.
@JoinColumn chooses the foreign-key column.
mappedBy names the Java property on the owning side. It does not name a database column.
In a bidirectional relationship, update both Java sides so the in-memory objects agree. Changing only the inverse collection does not set the owning foreign-key reference.

example.title: Map one user to many posts
description: Use these as AppUser.java and Post.java under the application package.
The relationship is bidirectional: AppUser holds posts and Post holds its author.
Create the tables through a migration, or use ddl-auto=create only for a disposable learning database.
explanation: Post.author owns the relationship. The posts table stores author_id.
AppUser.posts uses mappedBy="author" to refer to the same relationship.
addPost updates both objects. Save the user and post explicitly because this mapping has no cascade.
LAZY defers loading the author when supported by the provider. Fetching is covered separately.

richText: Cascade and deletion
A cascade applies a persistence operation on one entity to its related entities.
CascadeType.PERSIST propagates persist. MERGE propagates merge. REMOVE propagates remove.
CascadeType.ALL includes all cascade operations, including removal. Use it only when every propagated operation fits the relationship.
orphanRemoval=true removes a child when it is removed from an owned one-to-many collection or one-to-one relationship.
Cascading, orphan removal and database foreign-key constraints are different mechanisms.
Avoid including both sides of a bidirectional relationship in toString or generated JSON output. Following both sides can cause repeated traversal.
